article.title: Christian Nationalism
article.author: H. Scott Prosterman
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. The political tsunami that brought new blood to the U.S. House and Senate also set in motion a fresh dialectic to challenge the nativist Christian Nationalist movement in the U.S. While U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has been a forceful “Christian Soldier” in promoting illegal Christian and Jewish settlements in the West Bank, Texas Senator-Elect James Talarico is one of the newly elected officials poised to re-direct that narrative. Convicted felon Donald Trump has benefitted from his alliance with white Christian nationalists, who perceive him as a modern-day King Cyrus , a powerful heathen sent by God on their behalf. Though Trump has shown to be the most unspiritual man to sit in the Oval Office, they bought his con because he also appeals to their sense of nativism, racism and exclusion. African-American politicians such as the Rev. Ralph Warnock (D-GA) in the Democratic Party have long appealed to a sense of Christian justice, and the late President Jimmy Carter famously combined his Baptist faith with center-left positions. Still, this fall’s crop of preacher-representatives on the Democratic side of the aisle are remarkable. Related: Trump’s Executive Order 13899: Jewish Identity, Free Speech, and Palestinian Rights. Now come seminarians such as Talarico, Kansas Senator-Elect Adam Hamilton, and Texas Congressman-Elect Frederick Douglass Haynes III with historic upset wins. Their political strength comes in part from their objections to the MAGA Christian Nationalist agenda, and its misapplication to justify Israeli colonialism. The movement that empowered Trump, and fueled the January 6 riots is now being challenged by Christians who “walk the walk,” rather than those who twist the teachings of Jesus into instruments of hate. The strength of Talarico, Hamilton and Haynes comes from their calling out how Evangelical Christianity has been misinterpreted to promote Trump’s very un-Christian agenda. Whereas Trump’s army of Christian soldiers violently stormed the Capitol to disrupt the electoral process, claiming divine empowerment; Pastor Haynes began his campaign by stating that Jesus opposed genocide in Gaza and anywhere in the world. Trump’s Christian soldiers are as devoted to the sanctity of firearms as they are to Jesus. The new wave of “walk the walk” Christian Democrats are positioned to challenge that position. Their election brings a welcome “ Christian counterpoint to the evangelical support for Israel that has long dominated the religious debate over the U.S.-Israel relationship.” They are deploying the momentum of the Blue Tsunami to counter that reflexive support for the Zionist enterprise and to reclaim modern Christianity for the actual teachings of the New Testament. The warped invocation of Jesus in Trump’s project has been a destructive force in American society, religion and politics. Anyone not invested in MAGA welcomes the new liberation theologians in the House and Senate. Though all three of the figures mentioned above take exception to various Israeli military actions, there are subtle but notable differences in their approaches. Let’s examine their theological and political backgrounds, which led to this historical moment. Talarico has been a vocal critic of Christian Nationalism, and called it “a cancer on our religion.” Though he studied at Austin Presbyterian Theological Seminary, he was never ordained. Talarico been a forceful advocate of economic justice, separation of church and state, and public education free of religious influence. He also opposes book bans, and supports affordable childcare and paid family leave. He opposes U.S. sales of offensive weapons to Israel, but supports Israel’s right to defend itself from Iran and other enemies. Talarico advocates disarming Hamas and a two-state solution that recognizes Israeli and Palestinian sovereignty. But he opposes the unlawful Israeli squatter-settlements, and their ongoing expansion.
